statement: A pattern of dots grows in diamond-shaped rings. Stage 1 is a single dot, and each new stage adds a diamond-shaped ring around the previous one, so the stages have 1, 5, 13, 25, ... dots. Which is the first stage with more than 1000 dots?

choices.misconception: I wrote the number of dots as 2n(n + 1) + 1, shifting the stage numbers by one.
I assumed the counts behave like square numbers and found the first square above 1000.
I found when a single new ring has more than 1000 dots, instead of the whole stage.
I found the right stage but reported its number of dots rather than the stage number.

hints: Look at the differences between stages.
The amount added each time grows by the same step, so the totals follow a quadratic rule. Find that rule, then estimate which stage first passes 1000 and check the stages either side.
The differences are 4, 8, 12, ..., so stage n has 1 + 4(1 + 2 + ... + (n - 1)) = 2n(n - 1) + 1 dots.

solutions.reliable: The ring added at stage n has 4(n - 1) dots, so stage n has 1 + 4(1 + 2 + ... + (n - 1)) = 1 + 2n(n - 1) dots. Check: stage 4 gives 1 + 24 = 25. We need 2n(n - 1) + 1 > 1000. Stage 22 has 1 + 2 x 22 x 21 = 925 dots and stage 23 has 1 + 2 x 23 x 22 = 1013. So stage 23 is the first. The transferable idea: when the differences grow steadily, the totals are quadratic, and an estimate plus two checks finds the threshold.
solutions.elegant: Stage n is two squares fitted together, n x n and (n - 1) x (n - 1), so it has n squared + (n - 1) squared dots, about 2n squared. So n is near the square root of 500, which is about 22.4. Checking 22 and 23 settles it.

whyOnTest: Figurate patterns at this level need a general rule, and the threshold question tests both the rule and careful checking either side.
